authority.title: Authority map
authority.summary: Find who can act, what they can request, and what must be approved before evidence moves.
facts: Rules snapshot

119th Congress, checked November 7, 2026. The map features selected committees and subcommittees. Confirm the current chamber rules, committee rules and any authorizing orders before using them, especially when a new Congress organizes.
What this map does
It links to official authority and model work documents. A role or a link does not confer investigative power.
choices: house
Start with House Rule X and the specific committee’s jurisdiction, then check Rule XI and the committee’s procedures.
senate
Start with Senate Rule XXV jurisdiction and Rule XXVI procedure, then check the committee’s rules.
review
The originating office must document its lawful source and any restrictions before sharing evidence with an authorized review team.
coordination
Counsel may verify a possible state-law nexus and approved points of contact before any transfer of evidence.
congressional-action
A committee can use its authorized legislative tools based on reviewed findings, within its jurisdiction and applicable rules.

house.title: House
house.summary: Choose a committee by the legislative question and the program involved.
facts: Starting rule
House Rule X assigns jurisdiction. Rule XI sets baseline procedure for hearings, subpoenas and executive-session material.
Overlapping work
Identify the committee with a legislative purpose and document coordination with other committees. Each committee acts under its own authorization.
Disclosure
House Rule XI, clause 2(k)(7), governs release or public use of evidence taken in executive session. Committee authorization for covered material is separate from authority to request it.
choices: house-financial-services
Match the inquiry to financial institutions, securities or another subject within House Financial Services jurisdiction.
house-judiciary
Match the question to federal law, court administration, civil liberties or another Judiciary subject.
house-oversight
Check Rule X’s government management and special oversight jurisdiction and identify any committee with overlapping authority.
review
House custody and disclosure restrictions travel with the evidence. A hearing or request approval does not by itself authorize transfer.

senate.title: Senate
senate.summary: Choose a committee by its Senate jurisdiction and procedural rules.
facts: Starting rule
Senate Rule XXV assigns standing committee jurisdiction. Rule XXVI permits investigations and procedural tools within that jurisdiction. Each committee publishes its own rules.
Overlapping work
Identify which office may make requests, who may authorize a subpoena and who controls disclosure. House and Senate approvals remain separate.
Disclosure
An office considering outside disclosure must check Senate and committee confidentiality rules and any restrictions attached to the evidence.
choices: senate-judiciary
Match the legislative question to the administration of justice, constitutional rights or another Judiciary subject.
senate-hsgac
Match the legislative question to government operations or another topic within HSGAC’s authority.
review
Senate committee confidentiality, record ownership and required approvals govern what the originating office can share.

house-judiciary-approvals.title: Who must approve?
house-judiciary-approvals.summary: Under Rule IV, the committee chair may authorize and issue a subpoena after consulting the ranking minority member. The chair normally provides the draft at least one calendar day before issuance. A committee or subcommittee vote is a separate route and requires a majority present and a majority of those voting in favor.

senate-psi.title: Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations
senate-psi.summary: PSI examines government efficiency and economy and other matters within its delegated investigative jurisdiction.
facts: Open an investigation
PSI Rule 1 requires approval from the subcommittee chair and ranking minority member, with notice to all subcommittee members.
Hold a public hearing
Rule 1 permits approval by the chair and ranking member or a subcommittee majority. If all minority members object, a full committee majority must approve. Check the advance notice rule.
Request compulsory records

PSI Rule 2 allows authorization and issuance by the subcommittee chair or a designated subcommittee member, with notice. Check its 48-hour rule and the parent Rule 8(E) notice and timing conditions before issuance.
